claims.text: The starting material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi high-entropy-alloy thin film prepared by magnetron co-sputtering.
Combined argon–nitrogen annealing, cyclic tensile strain, and nanoribbon patterning will reduce internal residual stresses.
The combined treatment will refine the grain-boundary network.
Reduced residual stress and a refined grain-boundary network will produce a smoother and more homogeneous magnetostructural transition.
A smoother, more homogeneous magnetostructural transition will decrease hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The treatment can reduce hysteresis while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect.
Localized strain concentrations and defects act as nucleation barriers for the magnetostructural transition.
Relaxing localized strain and minimizing defects will make the transformation more spatially distributed and less abrupt.
A more distributed and less abrupt transformation will reduce hysteresis while maintaining substantial entropy change.
Treated samples will have a broader magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Treated samples will have lower hysteretic losses than the as-deposited baseline.
Nanoribbon-patterned treated samples will have improved heat-exchange properties.
The entropy-change magnitude after treatment will remain sufficiently high for effective magnetic refrigeration.
As-deposited films exhibit a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
As-deposited films exhibit a large entropy change and high hysteresis.
As-deposited films have limited heat-exchange rates because of bulk-like geometry.
The prediction is limited to non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys made by magnetron co-sputtering in geometries permitting surface-to-volume enhancement.
The hysteresis reduction and entropy-change trade-off depend on annealing conditions, tensile-strain parameters, and geometry scale.
